experiment_scope.stimulus: deuterium ion bombardment of a palladium target; nominal sheath acceleration reported as 30 keV
experiment_scope.electrochemical_condition: in-situ deuterium loading from heavy-water electrolyte

energy_boundary.note: paper explicitly states this apparatus is not net energy

campaigns.reconciliation_status: open; printed phase-I/phase-II saturation rates are 135.5(5) and 156.7(4) n/s, while the article separately reports a 15.1(1)% campaign increase; preserve both and resolve the estimator using source time series/analysis code

source-confirmed: Phase I is 138.6(3) n/s and Phase II is 164.3(13) n/s; the separately reported 18.5(2)% percentage is retained as its own paper claim

aggregate.unweighted_mean_status: derived arithmetic check only; not asserted to be authors' estimator

limitations: This fixture contains values stated in the published paper, not raw observations.
The Zenodo archive contents and DOI relationship have not yet been independently resolved.
Rounded rate pairs and source-reported percent changes are kept as separate claims because direct division does not reproduce every printed campaign percentage.
The D/Pd ratio during fusion was not directly measured in each fusion run; the paper relates it to separate in-situ XRD characterization.
This result is accelerator-driven D-D fusion and does not demonstrate cold fusion, excess-energy generation, or net energy.
The full article text and Supplementary Information cross-check confirm the third campaign Phase I saturation rate is 138.6(3) n/s (uncertainty 0.3), not 138.6(13). Phase II is 164.3(13) n/s.

background.condition: pre-experiment background measurement; paper also reports a stable background over 24 hours

repeated_beam_loading.condition: D+ beam loading at -30 kV and 0.2 mA after 120 minutes of reactor operation

isotope_control.electrolyte: 2 M K2CO3 in H2O instead of D2O
isotope_control.interpretation: D2O/H2O isotope control; paper attributes difference to D vs H loading, while exact fuel composition in each fusion run was not directly measured

beam_voltage_off_control.condition: sheath voltage turned off after steady beam-loading state
beam_voltage_off_control.note: Supplementary Note 6 reports return to background when beam voltage is turned off; this supports beam-driven lattice reaction rather than accelerator-free electrochemical LENR

electrochemical_cycle_off_on.note: During the reported cycle, rate varied by no more than 2% during electrochemical off periods; reactivation produced a smaller increase than the initial electrochemical-loading cycle

fuel_state_measurement_limit.interpretation: Paper explicitly states D/Pd during fusion was not directly measured; it assumes a similar ratio from independent in-situ XRD characterization.
